notes:
The three song pages are KEY ITEMS, not items: the wiki writes them as Item:"Un Moment" but bullet 4 calls them key items, and the resolver settles it -- only the ki table has them, and only WITH the literal quotation marks around the name (ids 339/340/341). The bare forms resolve to nothing at all, so the quotes are kept verbatim.

Bullet 3 is one instruction covering three zones, so it splits into three steps sharing a group -- the page gives no order and there is none. "Un Moment" is in Castle Zvahl Baileys OR Castle Zvahl Keep, and that is the one thing here that cannot be modelled: a step has one zone, and making it two steps is not a way out, because both would have to carry "Un Moment" as evidence and duplicate evidence is a hard demotion. Baileys is recorded and the Keep lives in the note.

Bullet 1 is a precondition, not a step. Bullets 4 and 5 are one visit to Carmelo split by a zone-out; both rungs point at the same NPC and neither is observable, so they merge into one turn-in with the zone-out in the note.

VERIFY: demoted to medium. Step 2's zone is a coin flip the schema cannot hold -- the page says Castle Zvahl Baileys OR Castle Zvahl Keep, and half the time the recorded marker is in the wrong zone. The draft flagged or_branch_unmodelled and then kept high anyway; an unmodellable branch that decides where a marker is drawn is exactly the medium case. Nothing else here is wrong: the three pages are distinct key items, each is obtained at its own step, the source order is preserved and every name resolves with the quotes kept.

notes:
Three bullets, exactly one of which is a step. The quest is a single trade.

The real gate is Monster Rearing level 2, which is reached by tending Mog Garden creatures day after day once you hold "Sakura and the Magic Spoon". Nothing in the packets reports a Monster Rearing rank, and that key item does not resolve against res/key_items.lua at all, so the gate is recorded only in prose -- which is why this is medium and not high. The ladder itself is not in doubt.

The header's giver, the Green Thumb Moogle, is never mentioned by the walkthrough; the only entity you touch is Chacharoon. The Moogle is kept as start because it resolves, it is a real standing NPC in the Mog Garden, and the page gives no positive contradiction -- only silence. Bullet 3 and its sub-bullet are outcomes: the "Discuss a cheering effect" option and the automatic [KI] Cheer: Lamb are what completing the quest hands you, and by the reward rule the Cheer key item is not used as evidence even though it resolves (2716).

notes:
The page forks on something no packet can see: whether you OPENED the key item and read it. Bullets 3-5 are the read branch, bullets 6-8 the unread branch, and the two share a spine -- Tami, then Zelman in Zeruhn Mines at (I-8), then back to Tami. Zelman's two bullets are one step carrying both citations.

The fork is modelled where it actually differs. The Meat Jerky purchase from Griselda is the read branch's extra errand, so it is optional; the return to Tami takes nothing on the unread branch and the jerky on the read branch, which is precisely items=[] with the jerky in items_alt.

Griselda's step carries NO evidence on purpose. Meat Jerky is a cheap, commonly-carried vendor food, and using it as evidence would jump the mark past Zelman for anyone who happened to have some in the bag. Tami's note is the one honest evidence point.

Reading the note also ends the quest's repeatability, which the header still reports as Yes; the header describes the unread path and is kept.
